findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock
findings.body: The cache is read under RLock, the lock is released, and then the write lock is taken without checking the cache again. At startup, or whenever the cache is nil, every concurrent caller sees nil. Each one then queues on `Lock()` and re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json one after another, even though the first caller has already filled the cache. In Dev mode every request takes the exclusive lock and does file I/O while holding it (and potentially an HTTP fetch if the CDN branch is enabled), which serializes all callers. A second check of `entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev` right after `Lock()` would avoid the redundant reloads.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test. A test that calls `GetWebAssets` from many goroutines, run under `go test -race`, would show the race is fixed and stop it coming back. The package has no such coverage, so a later change to the cache logic could silently reintroduce the race.
